problem_summary.summary: Return a longest contiguous substring that reads the same from left to right and right to left.
problem_summary.input_output: Input: a non-empty string s. Return any longest palindromic substring; multiple answers may be valid.
constraints: s contains only digits and English letters

brute_force.explanation: Try every substring and test its characters from both ends moving inward. Keep the longest substring found. This exhaustive method is straightforward for small inputs but repeats many character comparisons.
brute_force.correctness_idea: Every possible contiguous substring is examined, and each is accepted exactly when all mirrored character pairs match; therefore the longest accepted candidate is a longest palindrome.
brute_force.time_complexity: O(n^3): there are O(n^2) substrings and each palindrome check takes O(n) in the worst case.
brute_force.space_complexity: O(1) auxiliary space, excluding the returned substring.

optimized.explanation: Build a boolean table where dp[left][right] says whether that interval is a palindrome. An interval is palindromic when its endpoints match and its interior is empty, one character, or already known to be a palindrome. Process left indices downward so the interior state is ready.
optimized.correctness_idea: The endpoint-and-interior condition is necessary and sufficient for a substring to be a palindrome. Considering every interval and retaining the longest true one therefore finds a longest palindromic substring.
optimized.time_complexity: O(n^2), considering each substring interval once.
optimized.space_complexity: O(n^2) auxiliary space for the palindrome table.

steps.event: Start with the longest known single-character palindrome.
steps.action: Mark diagonal entries true as their left index is processed.

steps.condition: Endpoints match and the one-character interior is palindromic.
steps.action: Mark palindrome[1][3] true and update the best interval.

edge_cases.handling: The initial best interval is the entire one-character string.
The method returns one character, which is always a palindrome.
Matching endpoints and true interior states extend palindromes across the repeated run.
The implementation keeps the first maximum encountered; any longest answer is accepted.
